paper.title: Multi-Access Communications with Energy Harvesting: A Multi-Armed Bandit Model and the Optimality of the Myopic Policy

settings.name_in_paper: Non simultaneous energy harvesting and data transmission (restless multi-armed bandit)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless (Markovian) bandit / POMDP scheduling with known model; optimality of the myopic policy against the Bayes-optimal policy, not a learning regret problem.
unmapped: N arms (nodes), K plays per round (multiple plays)
the learner knows the Markov transition probabilities p_ij, e_0, operativity probability p and battery size B
finite-horizon discounted reward with discount factor beta
arm state = (EH Markov state, battery level); played arm's state reset after activity
settings.definition_quote: In this section we assume that the nodes are not able to harvest energy and transmit data simultaneously, and that if node~$i$ is active in TS~$n-1$, then its EH state in TS~$n$, $E_i^s(n)$, is either $0$ or $1$ with probabilities $e_0$ and $e_1$, respectively, independent of the EH state in TS~$n-1$, where $e_0 \leq \frac{p_{10}}{p_{01}+p_{10}}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Simultaneous energy harvesting and data transmission with batteryless nodes
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless (Markovian) bandit / POMDP scheduling with known model; optimality of the myopic policy, not a learning regret problem.
unmapped: N arms (nodes), K plays per round (multiple plays)
two-state Markov arms; learner knows transition probabilities p_11, p_01 and p
played arm observed only with probability p (imperfect sensing)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the nodes cannot store energy, and the harvested energy is lost if not used immediately. ... Energy available for transmission in TS~$n$ is equal to the energy harvested in TS~$n-1$, that is, $B_i(n)=E_i^h(n-1)$.

conditions: R(.) is a bounded regular function
tau(.) is a monotonically increasing contracting map

source.label: thm:1
source.quote: If $R(\cdot)$ is a bounded regular function, $\tau(\cdot)$ a monotonically increasing contracting map, $ \beta \leq 1$, and $\Delta_{l} \geq \Delta_{u} \beta p \frac{1-( \beta (1-p))^{T+1}}{1-\beta(1-p)}$, then MP is the optimal policy.

results.notes: Optimality statement encoded as zero loss of expected discounted reward relative to the optimal policy; general restless-bandit result.

source.label: thm:2
source.quote: For the reward function $R(\cdot)$ defined in (\ref{eq:reward}), if the transition probabilities satisfy $p_{11} \geq p_{01}$ and $e_{0} \leq \frac{p_{10}}{p_{01}+p_{10}}$, then MP is the optimal policy.

results.notes: Optimality of the myopic policy (expected discounted throughput) encoded as zero gap to optimal policy.

conditions: reward R = p * sum of belief states of scheduled nodes

source.label: thm:3
source.quote: If the reward function is $R(\mathcal{K}(n))=p\sum_{i\in\mathcal{K}(n)}s_i(n)$, and $p_{11} \geq p_{01}$, MP is the optimal policy.

results.notes: Optimality statement encoded as zero gap; proof only sketched in the paper.
